nodes.title: Amazon VPC: Key Ideas
nodes.content: A VPC is a logically isolated network inside an AWS region. You define the IP range, create subnets in multiple AZs, route tables decide where packets go, and security groups + NACLs filter what's allowed. Most networking exam Qs are VPC-shaped.

flashcards.front: Public vs private subnet — what makes the difference?
flashcards.back: Routing. A 'public' subnet has a route to an Internet Gateway (0.0.0.0/0 → IGW). A 'private' subnet doesn't — its instances can reach the internet only via a NAT Gateway (outbound) or VPC endpoint (to specific AWS services). The subnet's CIDR doesn't determine its category — the route table does.

flashcards.front: Security group vs network ACL — when do you use each?
flashcards.back: Security group: stateful (return traffic auto-allowed), applied per ENI / instance, default deny, allow rules only. NACL: stateless (must allow return traffic explicitly), applied per subnet, supports allow and deny rules, evaluated in numbered order. SGs handle 95% of cases; NACLs add a deny-list at the subnet edge.

Lets instances in a private subnet initiate outbound internet traffic (package updates, API calls to public endpoints) while remaining unreachable from the internet. The NAT replaces the source IP with its own elastic IP. One per AZ for HA — they're zonal, not regional.

flashcards.front: VPC peering vs Transit Gateway — when to scale up?
flashcards.back: Peering connects two VPCs (mesh: N VPCs need N×(N-1)/2 peerings). It's free per-GB but doesn't transit. Transit Gateway is a hub: many VPCs and on-prem VPNs all connect to it, full transitive routing. Use peering up to ~5 VPCs; switch to TGW when the mesh becomes painful.

pairs.stem: A company wants to use Interface VPC Endpoints (PrivateLink) to access Amazon S3 from within a VPC without going through the public internet. Which statement is accurate?
pairs.option: You can use S3 Interface Endpoints (PrivateLink) for cross-VPC or on-premises access.

pairs.stem: An application team exposes a Kubernetes service via an internal NLB in VPC-A. Consumers in VPC-B (different AWS account, same Region) must access this service privately without VPC peering or Transit Gateway attachments. Which solution is appropriate?
pairs.option: Create a VPC Endpoint Service (PrivateLink) on VPC-A's NLB and create an Interface Endpoint in VPC-B pointing to that service

pairs.stem: A company has a VPC endpoint (Interface) for an AWS service and wants to restrict which IAM principals can use it. Which mechanism enforces this at the endpoint level?
pairs.option: AWS RAM share permissions on the endpoint

pairs.stem: A company has a private ALB in a VPC and wants to expose it to customers over PrivateLink (Interface Endpoints). What must the company configure?
pairs.option: Create a VPC Endpoint Service directly from the ALB

pairs.stem: A company wants to enforce that all VPC endpoints created in member accounts must use an endpoint policy restricting access to specific S3 buckets. Which AWS service can enforce this at scale across accounts?
pairs.option: AWS Shield Advanced with endpoint enforcement

pairs.stem: A company has an EC2 instance in a private subnet without internet access. It must reach an Amazon Kinesis stream privately. What is the simplest solution?
pairs.option: Create an Interface VPC Endpoint (PrivateLink) for Kinesis in the VPC

nodes.title: Amazon CloudFront: Key Ideas
nodes.content: CloudFront is AWS's CDN — caches your origin's content at 400+ edge locations worldwide so users get low-latency hits. The exam tests origins, cache behaviors, TTLs, invalidation, signed URLs, and the difference between viewer and origin requests.

flashcards.front: What can CloudFront use as an origin?
flashcards.back: S3 bucket (typical for static sites), an ALB / API Gateway / Lambda function URL, an EC2 instance with a public IP, or any HTTP origin including on-prem servers. One distribution can have multiple origins with cache behaviors routing by path (e.g., `/api/*` → ALB, `/*` → S3).

flashcards.front: Cache key — what determines whether two requests hit the same cache entry?
flashcards.back: The cache key is composed from the URL path plus any policy-specified headers, cookies, and query strings. By default it's just path. To vary by `Accept-Language` for example, add it to the cache policy. Beware: too many cache-key dimensions explodes cache size and lowers hit rate.

flashcards.front: How do you invalidate cached content?
flashcards.back: Two options. (1) Cache invalidation API: pay per path invalidated — fine for emergencies, expensive at scale ('/*' is one path, but full bypass for ~15 min). (2) Versioned URLs: rename `style.css` to `style-v3.css` on every deploy — costs nothing, immediate, doesn't disturb the existing cache. Always prefer versioned URLs.

flashcards.front: What's a signed URL / signed cookie for?
flashcards.back: Time-limited access to private content. Signed URL: hand out a unique URL with a signature parameter that grants access until a specific timestamp. Signed cookie: same idea but the credential is in a cookie covering multiple URLs (good for streaming where the player issues many requests). Use IAM-based access (OAC) when content is non-public AND served only via CloudFront.

pairs.stem: A company has a CloudFront distribution serving content from multiple origins globally. They notice that requests during traffic spikes sometimes bypass the regional cache and hit the origin directly, increasing origin load. Which feature reduces origin load during spikes?
pairs.option: Enable CloudFront Origin Shield in a Region close to the origin to provide an additional centralized cache layer and reduce origin requests

pairs.stem: A company has an ALB behind CloudFront and needs to ensure CloudFront viewers cannot bypass CloudFront and hit the ALB directly. Which method provides this enforcement with the least maintenance overhead?
pairs.option: Place the ALB in a private subnet without a NAT Gateway so only CloudFront can reach it

pairs.stem: A company wants to monitor ISP-level performance issues affecting their internet-facing applications worldwide and automatically correlate them with their AWS resources. Which AWS service provides this capability?

A company uses CloudFront in front of multiple origins and wants to selectively modify viewer request headers (to add a geolocation header) before they reach the origin. Requirements: extremely low-latency, simple logic, no package dependencies. Which feature fits best?
pairs.option: CloudFront Functions running at edge locations for lightweight JavaScript manipulations on viewer-request and viewer-response events

pairs.stem: A media streaming company uses CloudFront with an S3 origin serving premium content. Requirements: (1) block direct access to the S3 bucket so that content is only accessible via CloudFront, (2) support signed URLs with short-lived tokens, (3) block countries under trade restrictions. Which combination implements all requirements?
pairs.option: Configure Origin Access Control (OAC) with SigV4.

pairs.stem: A company uses AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue public TLS certificates for ALBs and CloudFront. They want to automatically rotate certificates without manual intervention. Which statement is accurate?
pairs.option: ACM public certificates must be rotated manually every 13 months

pairs.stem: A global company uses Route 53 with latency-based routing and health checks for an application deployed in us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-1. Users in Singapore report being routed to eu-west-1 even though ap-southeast-1 is healthy. What is the most likely cause?
pairs.option: The ap-southeast-1 DNS record is missing.

pairs.stem: A company needs to share a Transit Gateway across 25 AWS accounts in an AWS Organization to attach VPCs from each account. Which service enables this sharing model?
pairs.option: Create a cross-account IAM role in the TGW owner account that grants ec2:AttachTransitGateway

pairs.stem: An organization requires that all outbound internet traffic from EKS pods in a VPC originate from specific static IPs so that SaaS vendors can allowlist them. Which architecture accomplishes this?
pairs.option: Deploy a Network Load Balancer in front of the outbound traffic

pairs.stem: A financial services company needs a hybrid DNS architecture where on-premises DNS servers can resolve records in AWS Route 53 private hosted zones, and AWS resources can resolve internal company domains hosted on-premises. What is the correct configuration?
pairs.option: Create Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoints for on-premises queries into AWS and outbound endpoints with forwarding rules for AWS queries to on-premises

pairs.stem: A company uses Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall to block requests to known malicious domains. They want high-confidence AWS-managed blocklists that are continuously updated. Which configuration should be used?
pairs.option: Associate the AWS Managed Domain Lists (AWSManagedDomainsMalwareDomainList.

pairs.stem: A customer has a VPC with CIDR 10.0.0.0/16 and needs to add more IP space without changing existing subnets. They also want to use the new space for EKS pods. Which approach is correct?
pairs.option: Add a /22 CIDR block from the 172.16.0.0/12 range, which is the only supported range for EKS
